name: Cat Litter Enclosure End Table
pitch: Hide the litter box in an end table: cut around your litter box, arch cat door, vented sides, a lift-off lid for a lamp or plant, and raised so the robot vacuum goes underneath.

stages.title: Cut the sheet(s)
stages.detail: Run the fit-test coupon first (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then cut 1 sheet(s) from the DXFs (CUT layer): 32 m of path, 36 vent slots. Inside-out order, air assist on.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush char from every edge, 120 then 180 grit; round over the cat-door edge and the lid edge by hand so there is nothing sharp at whisker height.

stages.title: Dry fit
stages.detail: Stand SIDE-L, push in BOTTOM, FRONT and BACK, add SIDE-R, then set the LID (with keys loose) on top. Check the litter box slides in and out with the lid off, and the door is square. No glue.

stages.title: Seal the inside
stages.detail: Litter and urine are the enemy of bare ply: give every inside face and the BOTTOM top 3 coats of waterborne poly or a 2-part epoxy, masking the tabs and slots. A removable plastic tray under the box is a cheap second layer.

stages.title: Glue-up (Titebond III)
stages.detail: Glue BOTTOM, FRONT and BACK into SIDE-L, add SIDE-R and clamp with cauls across the width. Check square by measuring the diagonals. Wipe squeeze-out at once.

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 16 #8 screws (3.0 mm pilots cut in): #8 x 1-1/2 in through the side faces into BOTTOM, FRONT and BACK; the lid keys take 4 x #8 x 1-1/4 in down through the LID (plug the heads).

stages.title: Lid keys
stages.detail: Glue the two LID-KEY strips under the LID so they sit 1 mm inside the walls (use the carcass as the jig), screw from the top, plug and sand. The lid then lifts off by hand for litter-box access.

stages.title: Finish, test, pack
stages.detail: Two coats of low-VOC water-based poly on the outside, 48 h cure and air out before it goes near a cat. Check a 15 kg lid load. Felt pads under the 4 feet. Flat-pack in one box about 0.7 x 0.6 x 0.12 m.

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) birch or Baltic-birch plywood, 4 x 8 ft (1220 x 2440 mm) x 1

hardware.item: Low-VOC sealer / epoxy for the inside (share of a quart)
hardware.note: interior is wet-area; included in finish too for the outside coats

materials.finish: low-VOC water-based poly outside, poly or epoxy inside (about $24 for both)

safety: Pet safety: no gaps a paw or head can wedge into (door is a smooth arch with no latch); keep the lid heavy enough to stay put (the lid weighs about 3 kg).
Seal the inside with a waterproof finish; urine soaks bare ply. Let VOCs off-gas fully (48 h minimum) before use.
Rated target 15 kg on the lid (a lamp and a plant), UNVERIFIED - do not sit on it.
Ventilation: keep the side vents unblocked. Not a children's product (no CPSIA testing).
Low piece (under 27 in): no wall anchor needed.

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed, machine time NOT measured on the real machine
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine time uses a sourced RANGE for a 120 W diode on 18 mm ply (low 120 / typical 300 / high 600 mm/min effective, i.e. after multiple passes; see CUT-SPEED-RESEARCH.md); ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate, so none of it is measured on this machine. Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).

machine_time.label: ESTIMATE. Diode = ACMER X1 Ultra 120 W on 18 mm plywood; effective rate = speed / passes. Includes rapid travel between contours and 15 min per sheet of load/focus/unload. Not measured.

commercial_laser.label: ASSUMPTION. Sourced case: 300-600 W CO2 flatbed, single pass at ~600 mm/min (vendor 480-720), 60 m/min rapids, 5 min/sheet, $8/h operating cost. What-if cases: a machine 10x / 20x faster than the diode mid cut+travel time (not sourced for 18 mm ply).

profit.price_band_source: My estimate: Etsy and Amazon cat-litter furniture runs about $90-$200 (mass-market MDF) to $250-$600 (solid wood/plywood handmade); SHORTLIST.md measured strong demand for pet furniture. Low = compact, one finish; high = XL for two cats, finished inside and out.
profit.note_machine_time: ESTIMATE: 2.1 h (low-speed case 4.8 h, best case 1.2 h) of machine time per unit for 32 m of cut path in 1 sheet(s) on a 120 W diode, 18 mm plywood. Machine time, not material, is still the limit on profit per hour, but a single test cut on scrap will replace this range with a real number.

unverified: Machine time is an estimate (120 W diode on 18 mm ply, sourced range, not measured on this machine); cut time and profit/hour depend on it.
Litter box sizes vary a lot: measure the exact box before ordering; interior = box + 50 mm in each direction.
Odor control of the vented design is untested; a carbon filter pad in the vents is an add-on, not modeled.
A French cleat is not offered: a litter box is too heavy and wet for a cleat; the piece stands on short feet raised for the robot vacuum instead.
Exterior (marine) plywood and cut quality of sealed inside faces are unverified.
Price band is my estimate, not a market quote.
